# dsh-web-start-ui · Startup Animation for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI
English | 中文
Startup animation for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Launch video skins · On screen before the shell paints · Click or Esc to skip · Its own settings pag
aunch video skins · On screen before the shell paints · Click or Esc to skip · Its own settings page
An extension for the DSH Web GUI and desktop client: the page opens on a **launch video** instead of
a cold, half-assembled shell, and the curtain lifts when the video ends. It ships two skins, accept
s your own uploads, and adds one first-level settings page (Settings → Startup animation). No DSH so
urce change, no third-party request.
## What it does
- **Playing before the GUI paints.** The host half contributes one inline script to the served index
.html, so the video element exists and is fetching ~30 ms into navigation. Measured on a 0.2.0-rc.2
host with the shipped skin: element at 3 ms, metadata at 211 ms, playback at 622 ms, while the GUI's

own first paint is at 191 ms — the animation is already covering it.
- **Adopted, not restarted.**
The browser half takes over that same `<video>` element, so the animation keeps its buffer and its `

currentTime` instead of jumping back to the start.
- **Lifts when the video ends** (and not before t
he shell has painted, bounded by a hold cap). A skin the browser cannot decode lifts on a safety tim

er instead: a broken video never becomes a wall in front of the GUI.
- **Two sources of skins.** Two
are shipped in the package; more can be uploaded from the settings page and deleted there again. Se

e Launch skins.
- **Skip on demand.** Click anywhere or press Escape to lift it immediately.
- **The
me aware.** It follows the shell's light/dark preference, remembers it for the next boot's early bac
kdrop, and honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.
## How it works
| Half | What it does |
| Host (`src/index.ts`) | Serves the launch-skin catalog and the video bytes (`src/host/routes.ts`:
list, select, upload, delete, and Range-capable asset GETs; mutations are loopback-only on top of th
e platform's own browser auth), and contributes the served index's early backdrop: a global with the
selected skin's URLs plus one inline script that paints the backdrop — and starts the video — befor

e the module graph is requested. |
| Browser (`src/client/index.ts`) | Adopts the `<video>` the host
started, wraps it in the curtain (the theme backdrop, the skip footnote, the outro), removes the ea
rly layer it is covering, and registers the settings section. |
The handoff is deliberately narrow: the early layer is `pointer-events: none`, one z-index step belo
w the real curtain, and it is removed the instant the curtain exists (the adopted video is moved out
of it first) — the outro fades to transparent, so a leftover backdrop would otherwise reappear as t
he GUI came back. A browser half that never loads leaves no dark window behind: the served row arms
its own 15 s removal timer.
## Launch skins
A launch skin is a **video**: one directory holding a `skin.json` manifest plus the video (and an op
tional poster frame). Video is the only medium — there is no style engine — so with no skin selected
nothing plays at all. Two sources, one shape:
| Source | Lives in | Gets there by |
| Built-in | `assets/launch/<id>/` in this package | `node scripts/add-launch-skin.mjs <video> --nam

e "..."` (`--poster`, `--duration`, `--name-en` optional) |
| Custom | `<DSH_HOME>/launch-animations
/<id>/` | the settings page: pick a file, it uploads to the host and becomes selectable |
The selected id is **host state** (`<DSH_HOME>/launch-animations/state.json`), so every browser of o
ne install opens on the same curtain — and the host can start the video *before* the module graph is
even requested: the served index carries the skin's URLs plus a small inline script that creates th
e `<video>`, sets `src` and calls `play()`. The browser half then **adopts that very element** inste
ad of restarting it (measured on a 0.2.0-rc.2 host: element at ~100 ms, GUI first paint at ~230 ms,
animated curtain ~600 ms).
**Selection.** A stored choice wins; with nothing stored (a fresh install, or an id whose skin was r
eplaced) the **first built-in skin** plays. Choosing *No skin* stores an explicit null, so the fallb
ack never overrides a choice. The asset route answers with an `ETag`, so a cached install revalidate
s with a 304 instead of re-downloading megabytes.
**What ships today:** two skins, both with a poster frame.

- `assets/launch/qinghua` — 青花瓷 · 水墨 (Blue-and-White · Ink), 12.28 s, 2024×1080 HEVC, ~16 MB.
- `ass
ets/launch/whale-senren` — 鲸鱼娘 · 千恋万花 (Whale Girl · Senren), 12.25 s, 2560×1440 H.264, ~44 MB. Its p
oster is frame 0, which is black (the clip fades in from black), so the curtain never opens on the e
me 0, which is black (the clip fades in from black), so the curtain never opens on the ending frame.
Together they are most of the package download (see Install) and well past the size budget suggested

## Settings
| Control | Values | Notes |
| Enabled | on / off | Off boots straight to the interface — and skips the early backdrop with it. |
| Launch skin | No skin · every built-in skin · every uploaded one | The video that opens DSH; uplo

ad and delete custom skins from the same page. |
| Replay | Once per session · Every load | `session

` writes a sessionStorage marker. |
| Click to skip | on / off | Escape always lifts the curtain. |

| Preview | button | Plays the selected skin once, right now. |
| Reset | button | Drops the stored
playback preferences and returns to the defaults. |
## Install
This plugin is standalone **on purpose**: it is not part of the `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` aggregate,
so it never arrives with the family bundle — install it where you want a launch video, and remove it
rives with the family bundle — install it where you want a launch video, and remove it the same way.
